summary: The study describes the fabrication of highly entangled hollow TiO2 nanoribbons using a biotemplating approach. A peptide nanoribbon framework was created from diphenylalanine, which was then coated with a thin layer of TiO2 via atomic layer deposition (ALD). The peptide template was removed by pyrolysis, resulting in hollow TiO2 nanoribbons with UV-switchable wetting properties.
evidence: A nanoscale layer of anatase TiO2 was deposited on the nanoribbon framework by means of atomic layer deposition. ... ALD is an advanced thin film deposition process that is applicable to arbitrarily shaped nonplanar substrates. ... The deposition temperature was 140 /C14 C ... The peptide template was removed by calcination at 400 /C14 C for 1 h under air condition.
